title: Literature refresh, executable-setup recovery, and a block-14 multi-agent plan (7 kept / 5 cut)

abstract: The block-15 multi-agent planning round's adversarial critic reported it could not find ATTNRES_ENABLE, NGRAM_WD_LAMBDA, or NGRAM_BACKOFF_KAPPA anywhere in the local checkout despite block-14 having reported concrete numbers for them. Direct verification confirmed the critic was right, and the defect had TWO independent causes, either alone sufficient to silently turn a treatment arm into its own control. (1) The three mechanisms never existed in the canonical train.py -- zero case-insensitive matches across 3358 lines, all five sota_snapshots, and the entire git history of the file; they lived only in forked one-off scripts on the remote box (repo/train_attnres_c1_v2.py, repo/train_c3.py). (2) The intervention records declared only descriptive lowercase parameters, so tools/run_gated.py:_arm_env resolved env={} and exported no flag at all. The gated runner still reported config_verified=True, because verify_config iterates the bound environment and an empty environment verifies trivially. The three block-14 deltas (-0.000839, -0.001281, -0.001019) are therefore not null results about AttnRes, C1, or C3; they are the same configuration measured twice, which is exactly why all three landed an order of magnitude inside the 2-sigma gate. They are retracted as invalid. The mechanisms have now been ported into the canonical train.py verbatim from the reference forks (each an exact no-op when off), a latent autograd bug in the reference AttnRes was found and fixed (preallocated stack buffers mutated in place invalidate the views backward requires; replaced with list+stack), all three flags are echoed in RESOLVED_CONFIG so config-verify can observe them, properly env-bound intervention records were added under new ids so frozen fingerprints stay valid, and two fail-closed guards were added to run_gated. A four-arm full-budget verification then produced large, unambiguous signal for the first time.
decisions: Retract the three affected block-14 results as invalid; they are not evidence about the named mechanisms.
Port all three mechanisms into the canonical train.py and echo them in RESOLVED_CONFIG so config-verify covers treatment flags, not only frozen run controls.

Register properly env-bound intervention records under NEW ids rather than bumping existing versions, so every frozen experiment fingerprint referencing the originals stays valid and history is not rewritten.
Make run_gated fail closed when a treatment intervention resolves to an empty environment, and report a bound key absent from RESOLVED_CONFIG distinctly from a value mismatch.
Re-run the affected hypotheses through the gated launcher against the repaired harness before any adopt or reject verdict is recorded.

limitations: Established by code audit rather than controlled experiment; no experiment can distinguish a no-op treatment from its control by construction, which is why it went undetected.
findings.statement: ATTNRES_ENABLE, NGRAM_WD_LAMBDA and NGRAM_BACKOFF_KAPPA were absent from the canonical train.py and the intervention records bound no environment, so every treatment arm launched against train.py ran a configuration byte-identical to its control while reporting config_verified=True.

They must be re-run through tools/run_stage.py with paired seeds before any adopt/reject decision.
The flags-off arm reproduced the reconciled 10-seed baseline (0.939797, sigma 0.002036) to within one sigma, supporting the claim that OFF is a genuine no-op.
findings.statement: With working implementations, all three mechanisms regress substantially at the current 10-shard operating point: versus a flags-off arm at val_bpb 0.941657, AttnRes gives +0.0146, C1 at lambda=0.02 gives +0.0222, and the C1+C3 combination gives +0.0236 -- each 3.5x to 5.8x the frame's 2-sigma gate of 0.004072.

limitations: Observed directly in the first GPU smoke test after porting and fixed by appending to a list and stacking at use time, then re-verified crash-free at full budget. This matches, and plausibly explains, the AttnRes crash already recorded in paper 013's negative results, but that correspondence is inferred rather than separately re-measured.
findings.statement: The reference AttnRes implementation carried a latent autograd defect: preallocated (L+1,B,T,d) stack buffers written in place invalidate the sliced views backward requires, raising a version-counter RuntimeError.

limitations: The four-arm verification is single-seed and was not launched through the gated runner, so it establishes mechanism functionality and effect direction, not an adoption verdict.

Whether the mechanisms would help at a different operating point (for example 5 shards, where the memorizer-regularization family predicts its benefit concentrates) is untested here; the active frame's scope_key is frozen to the 10-shard split.
methods: Adversarial-critic report cross-checked by direct grep of train.py, all sota_snapshots, the read-only v3 reference checkout, and git history; a remote filesystem search then located the real implementations as forked scripts. The three mechanisms were ported into the canonical train.py at the corresponding code sites (GPT.__init__ parameter allocation, setup_optimizer param groups, GPT.forward block loop and n-gram VE construction). Each was verified by GPU smoke test at reduced budget, then by a four-arm 300-second verification run (flags off / AttnRes / C1 / C1+C3) on the shared H200 box, single seed 42, reading RESOLVED_CONFIG to confirm each flag was consumed.
negative_results: Three block-14 experiments are retracted as invalid rather than reported as nulls: exp_block14_attnres_r2, exp_block14_c1_10sh_r2, exp_block14_c1c3_r2.
Once genuinely executed, none of AttnRes, C1, or the C1+C3 combination improves val_bpb at this operating point; all three regress well beyond the noise floor.

The prior CUDA-graph capture rejection is unaffected by this defect: that arm failed by reproducible segfault under two different batch configurations, an execution failure rather than a silent no-op.

title: A no-op intervention defect invalidated a block of results; root-caused, deep-fixed, and re-measured

abstract: After repairing the no-op intervention defect reported last period, eight levers were tested with genuinely working implementations (AttnRes naive and refined, token-shift, C1, C3, C1xC3, sparse-grad, rowwise state, nGPT hypersphere). Every one regressed, and every one shared a single mechanical signature: it lost 80 to 150 optimizer steps inside the fixed 300-second budget. In a wall-clock frame that step loss is paid directly in val_bpb, so the mechanisms were not the binding constraint. Two corrections came out of that sweep: NGRAM_SPARSE_GRAD, recorded in this campaign's own notes as a 9.3 percent step-time win, costs 148 steps on the reference box, the deciding variable being the torch version (2.13 on the dev box where the win was measured, 2.9.1 here), so the lever is version-gated rather than universal; and NGRAM_STATE_ROWWISE is exactly free (delta bpb +0.00004, delta steps -1) while cutting optimizer state, so it is banked as headroom rather than claimed as a win. The block's central result then inverted the picture. Intra-document attention masking, implemented densely, is catastrophic (1.012956 at 522 steps); implemented block-sparse via FlexAttention at identical masking semantics it reaches 0.943750 at 1084 steps, a gain of -0.0692 val_bpb and 2.08x the throughput from an implementation change alone. Against a matched-backend control it is a confirmed -0.0111 over two paired seeds, 2.7x the 2-sigma gate, while simultaneously gaining 101 steps. A block-size sweep proved monotonic (64 better than 128 better than 256; 32 fails on a FlexAttention minimum-block constraint), and at BLOCK=64 the flex path recovers essentially the whole step gap to fa3. Six paired seeds against the fa3 baseline give a mean of -0.001415 with 6/6 the same sign and t=-3.45 (p about 0.018): statistically detectable, but well inside the preregistered 2-sigma adoption gate of 0.004072, so it is NOT declared SOTA. Finally, the hypothesis that doc-masking would rescue the memorizer-regularization family was tested and falsified: C1 costs +0.0222 with doc-masking and +0.0222 without it, so its harm is not about cross-document contamination.
decisions: Do NOT declare SOTA for flex doc-masking at BLOCK=64 despite 6/6 same-sign paired improvements: the effect is sub-gate.
Adopt BLOCK=64 as the flex doc-mask setting for any future doc-mask work, since the block-size sweep is monotonic and 32 is infeasible.
Retire the hypothesis that cross-document contamination explains C1's harm.
Correct the stored NGRAM_SPARSE_GRAD note to version-gated rather than universal.
Treat any future wall-clock regression as evidence about an implementation until its kernel is competitive, per the AttnRes and doc-mask trajectories.

limitations: Single seed for the dense arms; the effect size is far larger than any plausible noise, but the dense arms were not replicated because their cost made them clearly non-competitive.
findings.statement: At identical masking semantics, replacing the dense (B,1,T,T) document mask with a block-sparse FlexAttention BlockMask changes val_bpb from 1.012956 at 522 steps to 0.943750 at 1084 steps: -0.0692 val_bpb and 2.08x the throughput from the implementation alone.

limitations: Two paired seeds; both same sign and far past the gate, but this is the matched-backend comparison, not a comparison against the campaign's fa3 baseline.
findings.statement: Against a matched sdpa control, flex doc-masking is a confirmed win of -0.0111 over two paired seeds (-0.00923 and -0.01291), 2.7x the 2-sigma gate, while also gaining 101 steps.

limitations: Deliberately NOT promoted: a refinement smaller than the measured noise floor is not an adoptable result under this campaign's own rule, regardless of its p-value. Recorded as a promising sub-gate candidate.
findings.statement: Against the fa3 baseline, flex doc-masking at BLOCK=64 gives a mean paired delta of -0.001415 over six seeds with 6/6 the same sign and t=-3.45, which is statistically detectable but does NOT clear the preregistered 2-sigma adoption gate of 0.004072.

limitations: Single seed per arm; the two independent measurements agreeing to four decimal places is what makes the falsification credible, not the individual precision.
findings.statement: Adding doc-masking does not change C1's verdict: n-gram-table weight decay costs +0.0222 with doc-masking and +0.0222 without it.

limitations: All doc-mask arms run on sdpa because the mask path is gated on that backend; the doc-mask benefit (-0.011) nearly cancels the sdpa penalty (+0.012), which is why the fa3 comparison lands near parity.

Getting doc-masking to fa3 speed is blocked by a concrete obstacle: this build exposes flash_attn_varlen_func only as an autograd.Function, not as the low-level custom-op pair, and letting torch.compile with fullgraph trace into an autograd.Function is the documented cause of this box's historical segfault.

Several arms in the final rounds ran six-wide on the shared box; the observed within-round spread on a repeated configuration was about 0.0012, which bounds how finely these single-seed comparisons can be read.
methods: All arms run on the reference H200 at STOP_MODE=time, TIME_BUDGET=300, COMPILE_MODE=max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, frozen 10-shard split, seed-matched. Doc-mask arms necessarily run ATTN_BACKEND=sdpa because the mask path is gated on it, so a MODE=window control isolates the document-restriction effect from the mandatory fa3-to-sdpa swap, and every doc-mask claim is stated against a matched-backend control rather than across backends. Kernel refinement of AttnRes was verified by VRAM and step-time as well as val_bpb. The block-size knob DOC_MASK_BLOCK was added (default 128 equals the FlexAttention default, so unset is unchanged). Paired deltas were computed per seed and summarized with a paired t statistic; the adoption decision uses the preregistered 2-sigma gate, not the p-value.
negative_results: Eight levers tested with working implementations all regressed, each losing 80-150 steps: AttnRes (naive and refined), token-shift, C1, C3, C1xC3, sparse-grad, and the nGPT hypersphere residual.

The nGPT hypersphere residual was the cheapest lever tested (-36 steps) yet collapsed quality; its alpha sweep is non-monotonic with an interior optimum at 0.25, indicating a real mechanism whose residual-only implementation is a half-system.
NGRAM_SPARSE_GRAD is harmful on the reference box (-148 steps), contradicting a stored note that recorded it as a 9.3 percent win on a different torch version.
DOC_MASK_BLOCK=32 fails with an InductorError from a FlexAttention minimum-block constraint, closing the block-size direction at 64.
The hypothesis that doc-masking would rescue the memorizer-regularization family is falsified.

title: Block-sparse doc-masking: a mechanism recovered from an implementation artifact, and a falsified rescue hypothesis

abstract: This period tested nine interventions against the walltime_5min_h200 frame and adopted none. The productive output is a scoped quantitative law and the retraction of two of our own claims. A batch-size ladder falsified its own preregistered prediction (optimum B in [48,64] at val_bpb 0.921-0.925); the measured curve has an interior optimum at the incumbent B=72. Investigating why a 1.94x increase in optimizer steps degraded quality exposed a steps-versus-tokens degeneracy invisible to every prior block, because all of them held batch fixed, under which tokens are proportional to steps. Varying batch decouples them and the data select tokens: val_bpb = a - b*ln(tokens) with b in [0.046, 0.086]. This law then predicted, OUT OF SAMPLE, the five deltas of an entirely different lever (n-gram table size) with residuals of -0.00008 to -0.0016, and the residual itself pins the intrinsic quality effect of that lever at ~0.0007. Combined with throughput effects at ~0.01, this yields the period's governing ratio: intrinsic quality effects in this architecture live at 1e-3 while throughput effects live at 1e-2, so any mechanism costing more than ~1.5% step time cannot break even. That single ratio explains a nine-lever losing streak more economically than any per-lever account. We then over-corrected: observing that fitted tok/s is monotonically increasing in B, we predicted B=288 would clear the gate on throughput alone. A paired n=5 test of B=96 returned a null (mean -0.000406, 2/5 same sign, t=-0.37), falsifying that correction. The decisive detail is that B=96 processes more tokens in all five pairs (+3.5% to +9.0%) while its token-law residuals are positive in all five: the extra tokens arrive and the quality does not. The law is therefore scoped to fixed batch, not refuted, and the batch lever is closed on paired evidence in both directions.
decisions: Adopt nothing this period. No intervention cleared the 0.004072 gate and none reached min_seeds=10.
Close the batch-size lever. It is now bounded on paired evidence in both directions, with an interior optimum at the incumbent B=72.
Retire n-gram table capacity as a lever in this frame, and retire NGRAM_STATE_ROWWISE=1 as a throughput mitigation.
Scope the token law to fixed batch rather than treating it as general; report the two-variable dependence explicitly whenever batch is a free variable.

Adopt the admissibility rule that follows from the measured 1e-3 versus 1e-2 ratio: do not launch any mechanism whose step-time cost exceeds ~1.5% until the zero-cost and negative-cost surface is exhausted.

Retract the claim that B=72 is optimal because it is the MFU peak, and retract the subsequent claim that throughput rises monotonically in B so larger batch would clear the gate. Both are recorded in paper 017 rather than silently dropped.
Require that future papers lead with a Next Experiments section derived from a multi-agent propose-and-critique round; this is now encoded in docs/EXPERIMENT_WORKFLOW.md as a hard precondition.

limitations: The B=96 arm of this ladder was contaminated by a co-tenant and is excluded; the upward direction was tested separately.
findings.statement: The preregistered batch optimum was falsified: predicted optimum B in [48,64] at val_bpb 0.921-0.925, measured an interior optimum at the incumbent B=72 (0.928257), with B=48 worse by +0.0033 and +0.0060 on two seeds and B=32 worse by +0.0109 and +0.0087.

limitations: A single least-squares fit to one seed series returns b=0.0755, which is false precision given the pairwise spread; the range is the defensible statement.
Subsequently scoped to fixed batch by the B=96 result below.
findings.statement: Quality tracks total tokens processed rather than optimizer step count. Across the uncontended ladder arms the rank order of val_bpb matches the rank order of tokens exactly, fitting val_bpb = a - b*ln(tokens) with b in [0.046, 0.086] from four pairwise estimates across two seed series.

limitations: This is an inferential claim about prior evidence, established by construction rather than by a new measurement.
findings.statement: The step-count explanation advanced in the prior block was under-determined rather than wrong: every supporting experiment held batch size fixed, under which tokens are exactly proportional to steps and the two hypotheses are observationally identical. No number of additional seeds could have separated them.

limitations: The verdict is specific to the wall-clock frame; larger tables retain a small positive intrinsic effect, quantified below.
findings.statement: N-gram capacity restoration from 2^19 to 2^21 is refuted: all five treatment arms regress, monotonically in table size, by +0.0021 to +0.0140.

limitations: Both the fitting and validating experiments ran at fixed batch B=72; the out-of-sample claim is across levers, not across operating points.
findings.statement: The token law validated OUT OF SAMPLE. Fit on a batch ladder, it predicted the n-gram capacity sweep's five deltas with residuals of -0.00008, -0.00008, -0.00058, -0.00152 and -0.00160. Every regression is accounted for by lost token throughput alone, and the residual is the intrinsic capacity benefit at approximately -0.0007.

limitations: The intrinsic ceiling of ~0.0007 is measured from one lever family; a genuinely different architectural axis could exceed it.
findings.statement: Intrinsic quality effects in this architecture are ~1e-3 while throughput effects are ~1e-2, so break-even for a mechanism costing s step time is 0.06*(-ln(1-s)): 1% costs 0.00060 and 5% costs 0.00308. Any mechanism costing more than ~1.5% step time cannot break even against the largest intrinsic effect ever measured here.

limitations: Single seed comparison at one table size.
findings.statement: NGRAM_STATE_ROWWISE=1 does not mitigate optimizer bandwidth as premised: at table multiplier 256 it is SLOWER than rowwise=0 (194.06 ms versus 188.48 ms, MFU 15.27 versus 15.53).

limitations: The -0.003059 observed at seed 43 was reported at the time as a positive signal; at n=1 it is a single draw from a distribution whose spread is four times the effect.
findings.statement: B=96 versus B=72 is a null at paired n=5: mean -0.000406, sd 0.002473, 2/5 same sign, t=-0.37. This falsifies our own upward correction, which had predicted that B=288 would clear the gate on throughput alone.

limitations: Established at two batch settings above the optimum and two below; the functional form of the two-variable law is not identified.
findings.statement: The token law is scoped, not refuted. B=96 processes more tokens in all five pairs (+3.5% to +9.0%) while its token-law residuals are positive in all five (+0.0008 to +0.0048): the extra tokens arrive and the quality does not. At fixed batch tokens are proportional to steps and one variable suffices; across batch they decouple with opposite signs, leaving an interior optimum where tokens bind from below and steps bind from above.

limitations: Identified by code inspection against external documentation; the per-step cost has not yet been measured with CUDA events, which is the proposed next step.
findings.statement: The adopted fa3 varlen doc-masking path builds document boundaries with torch.nonzero, whose data-dependent output shape forces a host synchronization every step and produces unbacked symbolic shapes that hard-disable CUDA graph capture. Two further per-step host syncs exist in the training loop.

limitations: Attributed by elimination and the code's own recorded note on pool reservation; no allocator trace was captured.
findings.statement: CUDA graph capture is additionally blocked by memory: all three max-autotune arms died silently, consistent with approximately 25 GB of graph private pools on top of approximately 30 GB of n-gram tables. B=144 died with a CUDA VRAM error from the same budget.

limitations: Two seeds only; the effect is well inside the single-seed noise floor either way.
findings.statement: Disabling the per-step telemetry validation pass (VAL_LOSS_EVERY=0) is a null: mean +0.000852 across two paired seeds, with identical step counts at seed 43 (1947 versus 1947). The probe is not on the critical path.

limitations: The corresponding intervention (NGRAM_VE_LR_SCALE) showed no signal at n=1 and is under test at higher n; the observation is about configuration, not yet about effect.
findings.statement: The n-gram value-embedding tables are schedule-exempt (NGRAM_WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.0) and take full-rate gradient steps through the final step, including on second-epoch tokens, while every other parameter group anneals to 0.05 of peak. This is the maximal-memorization configuration of the module already known to be the sole source of the frame's data-limitation signature.

limitations: PROVENANCE: every run in this period was launched directly over SSH rather than through the staged scheduler, so none carries a gated-experiment binding or run_ record. The findings now cite weak quarantined_campaign evidence bound to exact source digests, but they are not provenance-complete active-challenge runs and must not be cited as adoption evidence.
The shared 8xH200 box carries co-tenants; three arms were quarantined on step-count and MFU signatures, and contention remains the dominant nuisance variable.
The token law's coefficient b is bracketed at [0.046, 0.086] from only four pairwise estimates across two seed series.
The two-variable law implied by the B=96 scoping result is not identified; only the sign of each binding direction is established.
The host-synchronization finding rests on code inspection and external documentation, not on measured CUDA-event timings.
No intervention this period reached the min_seeds=10 threshold, so no adoption decision is supportable.

The prior attribution of the step bottleneck to a specific function is stale: that function no longer exists in train.py, and the widely-cited '194k tiny kernels per step' figure is arithmetically impossible at a 2-3 microsecond launch floor and is almost certainly a capture total.
methods: All arms ran the frozen walltime_5min_h200 frame: STOP_MODE=time, TIME_BUDGET=300, one H200, val_bpb on held-out shard 6542, training shards 1-10 frozen, adoption gate 2 sigma = 0.004072 with min_seeds=10. Arms were launched concurrently on separate GPUs of a shared 8xH200 box and paired by seed. Because the box carries co-tenants, every arm was screened on a step-count and MFU signature before use; three arms were quarantined on that basis (one batch-ladder arm at B=96 whose step time read 195 ms mid-run, on-model, but finished at 278.5 ms with MFU decaying 19.9 to 17.58; and two arms in earlier blocks). In the confirmation round, treatment and control were interleaved across GPU indices so that co-tenant load could not align systematically with an arm. Throughput was modelled as t_step = F + c*B and refit from measurement. Token counts are steps times 2048B with gradient accumulation pinned to one. IMPORTANT PROVENANCE LIMITATION: these runs were launched directly over SSH rather than through the staged scheduler, so they carry no gated-experiment binding or run_ record. Integrity restoration binds the findings to weak quarantined_campaign evidence IDs and exact source digests. They remain measurements that can be re-derived, not provenance-complete active-challenge runs.
negative_results: The preregistered batch optimum at B in [48,64] was falsified; the incumbent B=72 is an interior optimum.
N-gram capacity restoration to 2^21 regressed on all five arms, monotonically in table size.
NGRAM_STATE_ROWWISE=1 is slower than rowwise=0, falsifying its bandwidth-mitigation premise.
B=96 is a null at paired n=5, falsifying our own prediction that larger batch would clear the gate on throughput.
VAL_LOSS_EVERY=0 produced no throughput gain.
CUDA graph capture via COMPILE_MODE=max-autotune killed all three arms on memory.
B=144 failed with a CUDA VRAM error.
NGRAM_VE_LR_SCALE at 0.5 and 0.7 showed no signal at n=1.
Doc-masking on the pre-retarget configuration is real and highly consistent (-0.002203, 10/10 same sign, t=-9.04) but sub-gate and therefore not adoptable alone.

title: Nine levers, zero adoptions: scoping a token-throughput law and two self-retractions on the batch lever

abstract: The first hour of generation 12 admitted no GPU work. Instead, the campaign completed the mandatory read-through, verified 167 unit tests, validation, strict audit, setup reconciliation, and hourly-report status, confirmed exact local/remote hashes, and inventoried physical H200 tenancy. Three independent proposer agents inspected the current code and evidence through architecture, systems, and training-dynamics lenses. They pooled 13 structural candidates and several explicit offline kills; a separate adversarial critic was tasked to rescore every candidate before paper 019 and any experiment. The strongest uncriticized possibilities are exact packer-sourced FA3 boundary metadata, document-safe n-gram contexts, a zero-initialized n-gram branch, and repeat-conditioned n-gram freezing. These remain proposals, not findings. The current default FA3 varlen document isolation is operationally promising but scientifically provisional because its historical direct-SSH measurements lack immutable RunRecords. No adoption or performance claim is made this hour.
decisions: Adopt nothing and launch nothing before the separate critic and canonical paper 019 are complete.
Keep the plateau rule: only structural mechanisms, not nearby knobs, may consume scored GPU time.
Kill tail-carry packing and BOS-target masking before GPU unless new offline evidence overturns their measured magnitude bounds.
Require every systems candidate to prove at least 4.1 percent whole-step throughput improvement offline before a throughput-only scored screen.
Treat a prospective document-mask reproduction, if critic-approved, strictly as provenance repair and a one-pair screen, never as adoption evidence.

limitations: This is an operational authorization fact, not evidence that any candidate improves validation BPB.
findings.statement: Generation-12 startup integrity is green: 167 unit tests pass, validate has no warnings, strict audit has no warning or error, setup reconciliation passes, and the hourly registry was current before its 08:40Z boundary.

limitations: Tenancy is time-varying and must be inspected again immediately before every launch.

limitations: No profile yet establishes that boundary construction or uncovered loader work is at least the 4.07 percent throughput required to clear the current gate.

limitations: The candidate rankings were still under independent adversarial review at the report boundary.

methods: Read the repository protocol and current-scope records in their mandated order, including paper 018 and the Recursive behavioral specification. Ran the complete startup integrity suite. BOS targets are only about 0.166 percent of packed targets in the proposer's sample; masking them is too small and too reward-hack-prone to justify a scored run.

findings.statement: The baseline registered in research/setup/reconciliation.json v31 (0.934930, n=10) is contaminated: the same fa3-varlen-doc-mask configuration measured on an uncontended host in an earlier session gives 0.929541 (n=10), a gap of +0.005390 in the wrong direction, and 45 of 48 runs in the contaminating session completed approximately 1147 optimizer steps against an expected approximately 2000 for the same 300s budget.

findings.statement: lib.py's DATA_DIR resolution used os.path.isdir('/data') as its only check for whether to trust an upstream data mount. On the new execution host, /data exists as a leftover directory owned by a different, now-unreachable user account, containing only a broken symlink at /data/tokenizer -> /home/user/.cache/autoresearch/tokenizer. This silently redirected all data and tokenizer loading to an unusable path and raised PermissionError only once tokenizer loading was actually attempted, well after RESOLVED_CONFIG had already printed and the run appeared to be progressing normally.

limitations: This is a planning document; none of its six proposals have been run. The predicted effect sizes are derived from the campaign's own token-throughput law and from first-principles bandwidth arithmetic, not from a new measurement.

Two proposals in the original two-agent slate (FlashAttention-4 on Hopper; Lngram latent-code memory) were dropped by adversarial critique on a logistics finding -- github.com is unreachable from the execution host -- rather than on a scientific defect, and should be reconsidered if a mirror becomes available.
findings.statement: paper_021 (AI_papers/paper_021_the_stale_comment_20260730.tex) proposes six MECHANISM experiments, each with a numeric falsifier and seven-axis novelty/provenance/validity/impact/reliability/feasibility/falsifiability scoring. Its lead proposal targets train.py:2547-2548, a comment stating that optimizer step-time cost does not affect val_bpb under STOP_MODE=steps -- true of the campaign's dormant fixed-step frame, false under the only live wall-clock frame -- which left a full-table state decay unoptimized in the sparse n-gram RMSProp path (train.py:2572, 2579-2581), predicted at roughly 19ms per step against a previously unexplained 15.0ms batch-independent term in the campaign's own throughput model.

limitations: check-setup was RED at the start of this period (reference-code drift from the prior session's edits) and remains unresolved pending a full re-reconciliation, which is now also required by the lib.py fix and the host change.

No gated experiment has been authorized or run this period. All infrastructure work (environment setup, tokenizer training, the lib.py fix) was necessary before any authorize-run call could succeed on the new host.

The contamination finding is reported at preliminary_observation strength rather than contradicted/supported because it has not yet been backed by a registered internal_run evidence record citing real run_ids; that registration is queued as part of the re-reconciliation work.
methods: Diagnosis of the contaminated baseline was direct arithmetic: the registered baseline.per_seed values in research/setup/reconciliation.json (mean 0.934930, n=10) were compared against the same configuration's paired-run values recorded in campaign_log.jsonl from an earlier, uncontended session (mean 0.929541, n=10), a gap of +0.005390. The contaminating session's own run records (research/experiments/runs/runs.jsonl, experiment_ids matching docmask_provenance and block22) show num_steps clustering near 1147 in 45 of 48 runs against an expected ~2000 for the same 300s wall-clock budget, consistent with GPU contention from over-launching concurrent arms. The lib.py bug was found by running a smoke-test training step on the new host and tracing a PermissionError back to lib.py's DATA_DIR resolution, which trusted os.path.isdir('/data') without checking the directory actually contained usable files -- on this shared host /data is a leftover, unwritable symlink farm from a different (unreachable) account. The mechanism proposals in paper_021 were generated by two independent proposer agents (kernel/throughput lens and architecture/memory lens) reasoning from the actual train.py source plus the campaign's own recorded evidence, then screened by inline adversarial critique that eliminated two proposals on a logistics fact (github.com is unreachable from this host, blocking FlashAttention-4 and Lngram installation) discovered while writing the paper.
